About

Structured thinker, first — designer, second. The output is the same either way.

"I write the system before I design the screen."

MCA candidate at K. J. Somaiya Institute of Management, Somaiya Vidyavihar University, currently completing a six-month UI/UX Design internship at T&M AI and IT Solutions. Before that, a B.Com — commerce background, not a design-school one, which shows up in how I work: requirement documents and written specs before pixels.

Alongside the internship I ran a 30-day longitudinal study on emotional variation across the menstrual cycle, wrote it up as a paper now under peer review, and designed the product from its findings. That is the part of my work I would most want to be asked about: it is the only project where I owned the research as well as the design, and it is where I learned to state what the data cannot support.

Four of seven builds were HR-tech, which is why the employee lifecycle — hiring, onboarding, attendance, exit — is the domain I can talk about in most depth. Alongside them: two marketing sites, the AI Vision21 corporate site and the HireVision showcase.

How the work was validated

Honestly: stakeholder review, not end-user testing.

Method

Structured review sessions with the industry mentor, product team and domain experts — 2–3 rounds per module, with feedback triaged before anything got fixed. Nielsen's ten heuristics ran as a self-evaluation checklist on every module.

Critical Important Minor
Constraint

Limited direct access to real end users — a genuine limitation of an internship timeline. Persona assumptions were checked against proxy feedback from domain experts and product managers instead. That gap is stated here rather than implied away.

Outside the screen

Six things I do when I'm not designing — most of them outdoors, all of them habits.

I don't think of these as hobbies. They're the same instinct the work runs on: prepare properly, read the situation, then commit — and keep showing up on the days it isn't fun.

Cricket
Club, school, college, district
Competitive cricket across four levels, including a University of Mumbai inter-collegiate first place. Cricket rewards preparation and reading the situation before you act, which is roughly how I approach a new product brief.
Riding
Long rides, monsoon included
Ghat roads in heavy rain, in full wets, on purpose. Riding is the one thing that demands undivided attention — no notifications, no half-focus. It's the closest I get to a reset.
Trekking
Sahyadri forts and ridgelines
Western Ghats treks, usually in monsoon when the visibility is worst and the climb is best. A summit is the cleanest feedback loop there is: you either got there or you didn't.
Gym & cycling
Training on a streak
Structured training most days, plus night rides across Mumbai when the roads finally empty out. Progressive overload taught me more about shipping consistently than any productivity system did.
Sketching
Pencil before pixels
I draw — and not only wireframes. It's why my process starts on paper: sketching is where I find out whether an idea holds up before it gets the benefit of good typography.
Music
Live, loud, in a crowd
Constant listener, frequent concert-goer. A live set is a masterclass in pacing — build, hold, release — which is the same problem as sequencing a case study or a product flow.
